why: All three factual checks pass, but the finding is refuted as a divergence because it is an already-recorded product/scope decision in the parity audit itself. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: desktop.md line 428 contains the claimed sentence exactly (python substring check True). The whole line has two more sentences ('Preview uses this folder as its working directory, so if you selected a parent folder, subfolders with their own dev servers won't be detected automatically. To work with a subfolder's server, either start a session in that folder directly or add a configuration manually.') — they narrow scope to the session folder, they do not reverse the conclusion. The doc's field table (475-486), autoVerify default (450-452), autoPort tri-state (539-543), PORT hand-off (545) and the localhost origin-only/matching-port rule (517) all check out, so the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is a faithful reading of the page. (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/agent/browser-tool-runtime.ts:741 is `if (cmd === 'navigate') {`, whose body takes `parts.slice(1).join(' ').trim()` as a bare URL and calls `fns.navigate(url)` — it starts nothing. Correct as cited. (3) ABSENCE, NUL-SAFE: `grep -rna -a` for launch\.json|autoVerify|autoPort|runtimeExecutable over packages, apps, scripts, docs-site returns zero. The browser tool exposes 32 subcommands (open, navigate, snapshot, find, click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, upload, set-clipboard, get-clipboard, paste, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, window-resize, network, wait, key, downloads, scroll, back, forward, evaluate, focus, windows, release, close, hide) — none starts, stops, port-checks or auto-verifies a server. ONE LAYER UP/DOWN: the only `.claude/launch.json` in the tree is the repo's own at the root, consumed by the Claude Code harness (my own preview_start tool), not by our product — the claim already says this and it is right. The only 'dev server' hits in product source are apps/electron/src/main/window-manager.ts:114/287/340/380 and apps/viewer/vite.config.ts:30, which are the app shell's OWN Vite dev server for hot reload — an identically-worded sibling subsystem, not a user-project preview server. No upstream layer supplies the consequence. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions. REFUTATION: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md — the named source of truth — already rules on this at section 5e-2, lines 1719-1726: 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness: ... and the desktop product surfaces (preview servers, PR status, diff view, integrated terminal) that are product decisions rather than loop parity.' Preview servers are named explicitly and were deliberately assigned NO ROW. So the absence is real but it is a recorded product decision, not an unrecorded parity defect.
correctedState: Accurate as a statement of fact, wrong as a classification. There is genuinely no reader, writer or equivalent of `.claude/launch.json`, `autoVerify`, `autoPort` or the preview-server lifecycle anywhere in packages/, apps/, scripts/ or docs-site/ (NUL-safe grep: 0 hits), and browser-tool-runtime.ts:741's `navigate` takes a bare URL and starts nothing. But this is already a recorded scope decision, not an open gap: parity audit section 5e-2 (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1719-1726) lists 'the desktop product surfaces (preview servers, PR status, diff view, integrated terminal)' under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness ... product decisions rather than loop parity'. Two precisions to the doc reading if the row is ever revived: `PORT` is handed to the server only when Claude picks a port different from the requested one (desktop.md:545), not unconditionally; and a `configurations` entry carrying `url` with no command attaches the preview to a server the user already runs rather than starting one (desktop.md:521-532).
